page: Microsoft Azure E20ds_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EDSv5 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs derived from 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 160.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 768 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the E20ds_v5 in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks, with a Passmark CPU score of 25,791.42 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 11,082.0. However, its memory subsystem demonstrates strong performance, achieving a top-25% Passmark memory score of 2,776.57. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is measured at 117.04 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 62.5 GB/sec. For database operations, the server handles 19.85 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a Passmark database score of 9,990.96.

The high memory density and local SSD storage make this server qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads and database hosting, offering a balanced allocation of resources without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. However, performance tradeoffs are evident in large-scale machine learning tasks; while the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 269.68 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM, its prompt processing speed drops to a poor 4.19 tokens/sec for a large 70B model. Consequently, the E20ds_v5 is best suited for relational databases, caching layers, memory-intensive enterprise applications, and moderate data processing pipelines rather than large-scale LLM deployment.
description: Microsoft Azure E20ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, paired with 160.0 GB of system memory and 768 GB of local SSD storage. The hardware configuration delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, supported by a strong Passmark memory score in the top 25%. While the server exhibits average performance across standard compute benchmarks and struggles with large-scale LLM inference, it excels in memory-intensive operations, database tasks, and caching. The qualitative cost-efficiency of its high-density memory and local storage makes it highly suitable for hosting relational databases, enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing workloads.
